---
title: 'Tuturuuu Bot'
description: 'Owner setup, scoped automation identity and credential boundaries for tuturuuu-bot.'
---

`tuturuuu-bot` is a private GitHub App owned by `tutur3u`, installed only on
`tutur3u/platform`. Its webhook is inactive and it subscribes to no events.
The App separates automation authorship from `vhpx`'s human review identity.
This change supplies configuration; it does not create or install the App.

## Owner setup

Only the owner performs credential setup, outside agent sessions and recordings.

1. Review `.github/tuturuuu-bot/manifest.json`. Start the
   [GitHub manifest flow](https://docs.github.com/en/apps/sharing-github-apps/registering-a-github-app-from-a-manifest)
   by submitting that JSON as the `manifest` form field in a **POST** to
   `https://github.com/organizations/tutur3u/settings/apps/new`.
   A GET link alone does not submit the manifest. Use an owner-controlled form
   and callback, set a random `state`, add its `redirect_url` to a local copy of
   the manifest, and verify the callback state. Exchange the returned temporary
   code using `POST https://api.github.com/app-manifests/{code}/conversions`
   within one hour. This response contains credentials: route it directly to the
   owner's credential manager, never terminal output, git, chat or an agent.
   If no trusted manifest callback exists, use **Organization settings →
   Developer settings → GitHub Apps → New GitHub App**, transcribe this manifest's
   fields, disable the webhook and choose **Only on this account**. Generate the
   private key there as the owner. No callback service is deployed by this PR.
2. Confirm the available slug is exactly `tuturuuu-bot`; GitHub App names are
   globally unique. Confirm private visibility and the permission table below.
3. Click **Install App → tutur3u → Only select repositories → platform → Install**.
   Do not select all repositories. Record the installation ID from the install URL.
4. In **platform → Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions → Variables**, add
   `TUTURUUU_BOT_APP_ID` using the numeric App ID. Stage the private key first:
   save it as Actions secret `TUTURUUU_BOT_PRIVATE_KEY`, then enable the variable.
   Prefer a dedicated protected environment after migrating each minting job to
   that environment and testing its approval/branch restrictions. The current jobs
   use a repository secret; an environment-only secret will not be available yet.
   Do not add broad environment access just to make a skipped job run.
5. For local agents, the owner imports the key using Keychain Access into a generic
   password named `tuturuuu-bot-private-key`. Restrict access to the trusted launcher
   and owner session. Set non-secret `TUTURUUU_BOT_APP_ID` and
   `TUTURUUU_BOT_INSTALLATION_ID` in that session. Agents never receive or inspect
   the key. The helper reads it only in process memory using macOS `security`.
6. After reviewed code reaches its existing release branches, run one eligible
   release/dispatch job. Confirm the actor, repository restriction, requested
   permissions and automatic revocation. Check that resulting PR authors are
   `tuturuuu-bot[bot]` and all existing review/CI gates remain required. Test a local
   push to an owned feature branch and PR creation before retiring the old PAT.
   Do not dispatch production publication merely to test authentication.

## Permissions

| App permission | Why it is needed | Token restriction |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Contents: write | Release Please creates tags/releases and generated branches; local agents push owned branches. | Release job only; explicitly requested local tokens. |
| Pull requests: write | Release Please creates/updates release PRs; local agents create PRs. | Release job only; explicitly requested local tokens. |
| Issues: write | Release Please manages release labels and issue comments. | Release job only; explicitly requested local tokens. |
| Actions: write | Dispatch dependent package releases and TestFlight review retries. | Dispatch jobs only; explicitly requested local tokens. |
| Metadata: read | Required repository/installation metadata. | Implicit GitHub App baseline. |

No migrated consumer creates check runs: **checks:write is omitted**. There is
no workflows, administration, deployment, secrets or ruleset bypass permission.
No migrated job intentionally writes workflow files. Release formatting validates
its generated-file set; a future workflow-writing use requires a separate review.
The App must never approve PRs or be added as a ruleset bypass actor. GitHub's
pull-request permission also permits review APIs, so this is an operational
constraint, not a permission-level prohibition.

## Workflow trust and fallback

App minting uses SHA-pinned `actions/create-github-app-token`, with explicit
`permission-*` inputs and repository `platform`. The action revokes its token at
job cleanup. See the [action documentation](https://github.com/actions/create-github-app-token/tree/fee1f7d63c2ff003460e3d139729b119787bc349).
Only trusted main/production refs in this repository can mint. No App minting job
accepts fork events, `pull_request_target`, or untrusted checkout/code.

While `vars.TUTURUUU_BOT_APP_ID` is empty, the mint step skips and the consumer
uses its original token expression, including `RELEASE_PLEASE_TOKEN` for Release
Please. When the variable is set but the key/installation is invalid, minting
fails closed. It does not silently fall back after an authentication failure.
All workflow permissions, triggers, setup-node lines and existing gates remain
unchanged. Existing unpinned actions outside the inserted steps belong to the
separate action-pinning lane; this change introduces only a pinned action.

Release auto-merge retains its current PAT/GITHUB_TOKEN because it synchronizes
protected branches, including workflow files. Do not give the App bypass or
workflows authority to preserve that legacy path. Retire the PAT only after a
separate redesign and owner acceptance. Fork-visible comments, deployment
markers, OIDC attestations and job-scoped checks keep their existing tokens.
External Vercel, Cloudflare, Supabase, Modal, Turbo, Codecov and store/vault tokens
are service credentials, not GitHub PATs, and must not be replaced with App tokens.

## Local agent usage

Run commands from trusted code on an owner-controlled macOS host:

```sh
node scripts/tuturuuu-bot-token.js --permissions contents=write -- git push origin HEAD
node scripts/tuturuuu-bot-token.js --permissions contents=read,pull_requests=write -- gh pr create --repo tutur3u/platform
```

The helper accepts only `gh pr create` or `git push` children, explicit allowed permission names,
a numeric installation ID and the fixed GitHub API origin. It always requests
only repository `platform`. It signs RS256 JWTs in memory, rejects file/env keys,
does not offer token-printing modes and gives `GH_TOKEN`/`GITHUB_TOKEN` to the
child environment. Git receives temporary credential-helper config; the helper
never invokes `gh auth login`, `gh auth setup-git` or writes credentials/config.
Use an HTTPS GitHub remote; SSH uses the host's SSH identity instead of this token.
Use `--repo tutur3u/platform` for gh operations. Workflows cannot be pushed with
this helper's permission allowlist. No 1Password adapter is implemented.

The child exit status is preserved and the token is revoked on normal completion,
child failure or wrapper error after minting. Requests have 15-second deadlines;
the child has a 50-minute deadline. Abrupt termination, host failure or network
failure may prevent revocation; GitHub installation tokens expire within an hour.
The owner must monitor and revoke unknown outcomes instead of blindly replaying
writes. Authentication failures do not prove an earlier push/PR did not complete.

### Threat model and revocation

The trusted boundary includes the host user, Keychain ACLs, wrapper source, Node,
Git, gh, PATH, repository hooks/config and the child command. Do not run this helper
from an unreviewed checkout or expose its process/environment through diagnostics.
Malicious same-user code, child commands, hooks or debuggers can steal in-memory
keys/tokens. Child output is inherited: a deliberately hostile gh/git command can
print environment-derived credentials; the wrapper cannot sandbox trusted tools.
Never use verbose HTTP tracing, shell tracing, credential inspection, commands
that print tokens, or commands that persist auth. Keychain-only storage prevents
accidental repository/env-file leaks, not a compromised host. Child env receives
no App configuration or key; errors from signing, Keychain and API are replaced
with fixed messages so response bodies and exception text cannot leak secrets.
The helper performs no automatic retries and follows no API redirects.

For rotation, the owner creates a second private key in App settings, replaces
Actions/Keychain credentials privately, validates a narrowly scoped operation,
then deletes the old App key. Do not commit downloaded PEMs. Delete any temporary
owner download after secure import. Removing a key does not reliably revoke every
already-issued installation token: revoke those tokens explicitly or suspend the
installation. For emergency revocation, **Organization settings → GitHub Apps →
tuturuuu-bot → Suspend/Uninstall**; delete compromised App keys and Keychain items,
remove the Actions secret and clear the App ID variable. Clearing the variable
alone re-enables the old fallback and is not credential revocation. Revoke any old
PAT independently. Review the org audit log and affected writes before resuming.

## Human review

PRs authored by `tuturuuu-bot[bot]` are normal PRs. `vhpx` is a different principal,
so vhpx's approval counts as independent human review, subject to the repository's
rules. Commit coauthor trailers do not determine the PR author; authentication at
`gh pr create` does. This bootstrap PR may still be created by the existing
identity because the App is not provisioned yet. The bot never approves PRs.
The classifier remains owned by #6456 and is unchanged. Validate the live ruleset
and classifier after installation; source configuration is not runtime acceptance.

## Inventory and follow-up

The inventory includes workflows with write permissions, dispatch triggers, token
references, comments or release automation, and matching non-test scripts under
`scripts/`. Explicit job scopes are reported below. Read-only jobs and service
credential references are retained to make the audit boundary visible.
Regenerate after upstream workflow changes:

```sh
node scripts/ci/tuturuuu-bot-inventory.js --write
node --test scripts/ci/tuturuuu-bot-token.test.js scripts/ci/tuturuuu-bot-workflows.test.js
```

Reserved files: `discord-modal-deploy.yml`, `supabase-staging.yaml`,
`supabase-production.yaml`, `production-package-resume.yaml`,
`release-please-transient-retry.yaml`, security-checks and security-review-classifier
workflows, plus classifier code (#6459/#6456). They require owner-led follow-up
migration after their current PRs land. No setup-node or action-hardening changes
are included. CI on the exact PR commit and independent credential/security review
remain integration gates; mocked helper tests do not prove a live installation.
